record.original_question: For the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d and an integer m with 1 <= m <= 2^d, what is the maximum possible largest eigenvalue of the induced subgraph Q_d[U] over all vertex sets U of size m?

evidence.quote: Problem 7 (Fink, c.f. [21], Friedman-Tillich [70]). What is the maximum of the largest eigenvalue of Q_d[U], where |U| = m and 1 ≤ m ≤ 2^d ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_d$ denote the $d$-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^d$ and in which two vertices are adjacent if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate. For a subset $U \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$, let $Q_d[U]$ denote the subgraph of $Q_d$ induced by $U$, and let $\lambda_1(Q_d[U])$ denote its largest eigenvalue (i.e., the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix). For each integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le 2^d$, determine
$$f(d,m) := \max\{\lambda_1(Q_d[U]) : U \subseteq \{0,1\}^d,\ |U| = m\}.$$
That is, find a closed-form expression (or sharp characterization) for the maximum possible largest eigenvalue of an induced subgraph of $Q_d$ on exactly $m$ vertices, together with the extremal sets $U$ achieving this maximum.
artifact.category_tag: Spectral graph theory of the hypercube
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (attributed to Fink, with a weaker form by Friedman–Tillich) appears to remain open in general. Partial results are known: Bollobás and Lee showed that for an induced subgraph on $n \le d$ vertices with $n \ge 105$, the largest eigenvalue is at most $\sqrt{n-1}$, achieved by stars; and Hamming balls of radius $o(d)$ achieve a largest eigenvalue within $1+o(1)$ of the conjectured maximum. No complete solution for arbitrary $m$ has been published.

status_evidence.title: Eigenvalues of subgraphs of the cube — Bollobás, Lee
status_evidence.snippet: For an induced subgraph G of Q_d with n ≤ d vertices, for n ≥ 105, λ_1(G) ≤ √(n−1), with equality iff G is a star; Hamming balls believed to be near-maximizers.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results known; problem of exact maximum for all m remains open.

status_evidence.title: Eigenvalues of subgraphs of the cube — ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the problem of maximizing the largest eigenvalue of induced subgraphs of the hypercube; gives partial bounds.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem is treated as open with partial results.
